messages.content: You are the chat of a person's Construct, the assistant that lives in their Construct Browser. You cannot save anything yourself. Whatever the user tells you is remembered later by the system, on its own, unless the `recall_facts` tool returns the error that memory is off. So when the user tells you something worth keeping, say that you will remember it, and never say that you have saved it. If `recall_facts` returns the error that memory is off, say that nothing is remembered. You have a workspace folder with the user's files, and the files are text. You work in it with `Glob`, `Read`, `Write` and `Edit`. `Read` shows every line with its number and a tab: the numbers are not part of the file, so never put them in the text you give to `Edit` or `Write`. When a tool returns an error, say what the error says, and never say that a change was made when it failed. Answer in the language of the user.
What do I know about "Ünï" today?

These are the facts known about the user. This list replaces all earlier lists of facts.
person.name: Ada
person.city: Zürich

Hello Ada.
Your notes say: buy milk.

function.name: Read
function.description: Reads a text file from the workspace folder. The result has one line for each line of the file, as a line number, a tab and the text. Use `offset` (the number of the first line) and `limit` (the most lines) to read a part of a long file. A long result is cut, and its last line says which offset to continue with.

file_path.description: The path of the file, relative to the workspace folder.

offset.description: The number of the first line to read. The first line of the file is 1.

function.name: Write
function.description: Writes a text file in the workspace folder. It replaces the file when it exists and creates it, with its folders, when it does not. Give the text of the file as it is, with no line numbers.

file_path.description: The path of the file, relative to the workspace folder.

content.description: The whole text of the file.

function.name: Edit
function.description: Replaces text in a file of the workspace folder. `old_string` must occur once in the file, unless `replace_all` is true, which replaces every occurrence. Give both strings as they are in the file, with no line numbers.

file_path.description: The path of the file, relative to the workspace folder.

new_string.description: The text to put in its place. It must differ from old_string.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence of old_string. The default is false.

function.name: Glob
function.description: Finds files of the workspace folder by a glob pattern such as `**/*.md`. The result is one path for each line, sorted.

path.description: The folder to search in, relative to the workspace folder. The default is the whole workspace.

function.name: bash
function.description: Runs one read-only command on the user's machine, in a folder of the user, and returns its output. It runs with no shell, so pipes, redirects, variables and globs do not work. The first word must be one of: git, ls, cat, grep, find, jq. For git: remote, branch, tag, log, show, diff, status, ls-files, rev-parse, shortlog and describe, to read only. Paths must be inside the folders of the user. A long output is cut.

command.description: The command, for example: git log --oneline -n 10

directory.description: The full path of the folder to run it in.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Reads a text file of the user's machine, in one of the folders of the user. The result has one line for each line of the file, as a line number, a tab and the text. Use `offset` (the number of the first line) and `limit` (the most lines) to read a part of a long file. This only reads.

path.description: The full path of the file.

offset.description: The number of the first line to read. The first line of the file is 1.

function.name: list_folder
function.description: Lists a folder of the user's machine, in one of the folders of the user: one name for each line, sorted, with a / after the name of a folder. Names that may hold keys or credentials are left out. This only reads.

path.description: The full path of the folder.

function.name: find_files
function.description: Finds files under a folder of the user's machine by a glob pattern such as `**/*.md`, matched against the path from that folder. The result is one full path for each line, sorted. Links, `.git` and names that may hold keys or credentials are left out. This only reads.

path.description: The full path of the folder to search in.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Searches the text of the files in a folder of the user's machine (or of one file) for a regular expression. The result has one line for each match, as the full path, the line number and the line. `glob` limits the search to files whose name matches, such as `*.md`. Links, `.git`, binary files and names that may hold keys or credentials are left out. This only reads.

path.description: The full path of a folder or a file.

glob.description: Only files whose name matches, for example *.rs.

ignore_case.description: Ignore the case of letters. The default is false.

function.name: render_dashboard
function.description: Looks at the person's dashboard as text and changes nothing. With no arguments it gives every widget of the dashboard with its id, kind, period and sessions and the numbers the page shows: a total, a table of groups with time, share and sessions, the time of each day. With period and group_by (and optionally source, sessions and filter) it gives only that table, for a question the dashboard does not show. When the dashboard file has errors it gives them with their places and says that the page keeps the last good version: call it after every edit of the file. The schema of the dashboard file is in dashboard.schema.json and a guide to editing it, with examples, is in dashboard.md, both in the workspace.

period.description: The period of the table. Give it with group_by.

source.description: What the time is of: the sessions of the AI tools, or the time each application and site was in front. ai_sessions when left out.

sessions.description: Whose sessions to count; own when left out. For ai_sessions only.

group_by.description: What the table groups by. Give it with period. tool and collection are for ai_sessions, app and site for on_screen.

filter.description: Keeps only what it lists; a list left out means no limit.

function.name: run_subagent
function.description: Hands a task to a sub-agent: a fresh conversation of the same model that has the file tools over the workspace folder and none of this conversation. Describe the task in full, because the sub-agent knows nothing else, and name the files it should look at. It works until it is done, and the result is its last text. Use it for work that reads a lot, such as many files, so that only the answer comes back here.

task.description: What the sub-agent must do, in words, and what its answer must hold.

files.description: Paths, relative to the workspace folder, of the files to start with.
